Bachelor of 3D Art and Animation
description:
TAFE NSW frames this degree explicitly around commercial production pipelines rather than pure fine-arts animation theory. Students work in deadline-driven environments meant to mimic actual studio conditions in feature film, games, television, advertising and visualisation work, and graduate with a bachelor's degree plus a showreel built for client and employer review rather than just an academic portfolio. That production-pipeline framing runs through the whole course: students don't just learn individual 3D and animation skills in isolation, they practice working with others across a production pipeline to deliver a finished result against a brief, the way an actual studio team would.

Run out of Design Centre Enmore, one of TAFE NSW's specialist creative campuses, the degree blends theoretical grounding in art and animation principles with the technical software skills the games and VFX industries actually use day to day.

Graduates aim at roles across feature filmmaking, game production, television and online content, and advertising and visualisation, a broader placement than a games-only or film-only animation degree, useful for students who aren't yet sure which specific corner of the visual effects and animation industry they want to land in.
curriculum:
Core subjects: animation principles, 3D modelling and texturing, rigging and character animation, visual effects and compositing, lighting and rendering, art and design theory
Production-pipeline studio projects simulating deadline-driven commercial briefs
21 core subjects, 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Final-year capstone: client-brief production project, delivered as part of a team, contributing to a graduate showreel
Delivered at Design Centre Enmore; total three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma pathway, portfolio may be requested

name: Bachelor of Applied Commerce
description:
TAFE NSW's Bachelor of Applied Commerce carries triple professional-body accreditation: CPA Australia, Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CAANZ), and the Financial Advice Association Australia (FAAA). That's a heavier accreditation load than most standalone accounting or financial planning degrees carry individually, since it's built to satisfy the education requirements of both the accounting and financial planning professions at once. Students choose a major in accounting or financial planning, or take a double major covering both, a genuinely unusual combination given how differently those two professions are regulated and how rarely degrees try to service both simultaneously.

A third-year industry placement is built into the structure, developed in consultation with industry so the practical component reflects what employers in accounting and financial services firms are actually looking for rather than a generic business internship.

Coursework runs beyond pure numbers into client psychology and communication, reflecting how much of financial planning practice in particular depends on advising real people through decisions rather than just producing correct calculations.
curriculum:
Core units: accounting principles, financial planning fundamentals, marketing, client psychology and communication, management, economics, business law, taxation
Major (choose one or both): Accounting / Financial Planning
Third-year industry placement, developed in consultation with accounting and financial services employers
Accreditation alignment: CPA Australia, CAANZ, and FAAA education requirements built into course design
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
TAFE NSW's Bachelor of Business builds toward three named specialisations: marketing, management, or hospitality and hotel management. The placement requirement is deliberately scaled to match: 60 hours minimum for marketing and management students, but a much heavier 300 hours for the hospitality and hotel management stream, reflecting how much that industry expects hands-on shift experience before graduation. Students commit to a specialisation from second year, choosing four relevant electives in year two and another four in year three that build toward it, rather than declaring a major on day one and locking it in.

Coursework spans management, economics, finance, marketing, communications technologies, business statistics, law and people management, a broad general-business foundation before the specialisation electives narrow things down. Being a TAFE NSW degree rather than a university one, the course leans into applied, workplace-facing content and built-in professional placement as differentiators, consistent with the sector's practical training reputation.

Graduates come out with both a bachelor's qualification and documented, assessed workplace hours in their chosen specialisation, which matters particularly for the hospitality stream where employers routinely want to see real service-floor or front-of-house experience.
curriculum:
Core units: business theory and practice, management principles, economics, finance, marketing fundamentals, communications technologies, business statistics, business law, people management
Year 2: 4 specialisation electives (marketing, management, or hospitality and hotel management)
Year 3: 4 further specialisation electives, building toward the chosen stream
Work placement: minimum 60 hours (marketing/management) or minimum 300 hours (hospitality and hotel management)
Total: three-year bachelor's degree, specialisation confirmed through elective selection rather than a separate application
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (ATAR not required; portfolio/mature-age and VET pathway entry accepted) or a relevant Diploma/Advanced Diploma

name: Bachelor of Business (Hospitality and Hotel Management)
description:
This is the hospitality and hotel management specialisation of TAFE NSW's broader Bachelor of Business, and the placement load makes the distinction obvious: 300 hours minimum, five times the 60-hour minimum set for the marketing and management streams of the same base degree. That reflects how hospitality employers hire, since a degree without extensive documented shift and service-floor experience carries a lot less weight in that industry than one that does.

Students share the same core business foundation as other Bachelor of Business students (management, economics, finance, marketing, business law, communications technologies, statistics) before specialising into hospitality and hotel-specific electives from second year onward, so graduates leave with both general business competence and hotel/hospitality-specific operational knowledge rather than one at the expense of the other.

Given TAFE NSW's long history running vocational hospitality training (commercial cookery, hotel operations, tourism) alongside this degree, students in this stream often have access to industry connections and placement employers built up through the organisation's much larger hospitality training footprint, rather than a placement office that's improvising industry contacts from scratch.
curriculum:
Core business units: management principles, economics, finance, marketing fundamentals, business law, communications technologies, business statistics, people management
Year 2 hospitality and hotel management electives: front office and rooms division operations, food and beverage management, event and conference operations
Year 3 hospitality and hotel management electives: revenue management, hotel operations strategy, tourism and hospitality marketing
Work placement: minimum 300 hours in a hospitality or hotel setting
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway

name: Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance)
description:
This degree is the top tier of a deliberately staged three-year pathway: a one-year Diploma of Music first, in a student's choice of Sound Production, Performance, or Creation and Composition specialisation, followed by the two-year Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance) itself. That staged structure means students test their specialisation choice at diploma level before committing to the longer bachelor's stage, and it gives TAFE NSW a natural exit point for students who want a shorter, standalone qualification rather than the full degree.

Unlike a conservatorium-style performance degree that concentrates heavily on classical technique and repertoire, this program is built for working across performance, production and composition simultaneously, reflecting how contemporary music careers rarely stay confined to just one of those roles. The Sound Production diploma track, for instance, is explicitly aimed at assistant sound engineer and sound designer roles in the entertainment industry, while Creation and Composition leans toward electronic production, sound design and music distribution.

Students come out with both technical production skills and performance capability, positioned for careers as recording artists, producers, composers or session musicians rather than a single narrow professional track.
curriculum:
Year 1: Diploma of Music, one specialisation chosen — Sound Production, Performance, or Creation and Composition
Years 2-3: Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance) core units — music production techniques, live performance practice, composition and arrangement, music business and industry practice, studio recording and mixing
Elective units aligned to the student's diploma specialisation background
Final-year capstone: original creative project (performance, production, or composition portfolio)
Total: three-year packaged pathway (1-year diploma + 2-year bachelor's)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma pathway, audition/portfolio may be requested

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education and Care (Birth-5 years)
description:
This ACECQA-approved degree qualifies graduates as early childhood teachers, not just educators, which puts it in the same regulatory category as equivalent university early childhood teaching degrees despite being delivered by TAFE NSW. The four-year structure carries 805 hours (115 days) of work placement, a substantial practicum load that's woven through the degree rather than concentrated in a single final-year block, giving students repeated, staged exposure to real early learning settings as their coursework deepens.

Curriculum content runs across children's development, language and literacies, STEM, Indigenous education, leadership, inclusive and gifted education, health and wellbeing, and the arts in the early years: a broader spread than a narrower early childhood care qualification, reflecting the birth-to-five age range the degree is built to cover rather than splitting infant/toddler care from preschool teaching into separate credentials.

Because it's delivered through TAFE NSW's applied learning model, students combine contemporary early-childhood research with heavily practice-oriented coursework, which the university positions as a direct pathway into preschool and long day care teaching roles as well as broader children's and family services positions.
curriculum:
Core units across children's development and learning theory, language and literacies, STEM in the early years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, inclusive and gifted education, leadership and service management, health, safety and wellbeing, creative arts pedagogy
805 hours (115 days) of supervised work placement, staged progressively across the four years
ACECQA-approved sequence, required for recognition as a qualified early childhood teacher
Final-year capstone integrating leadership and service management with an extended placement block
Total: four-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care, plus a Working with Children Check

name: Bachelor of Fashion Design
description:
Delivered through TAFE NSW's Fashion Design Studio, a name in Australian fashion education dating back to 1955, this three-year degree ends with the sort of milestone most fashion schools treat as the whole point: in third year, students design and present their own collection and graduate holding a portfolio of realised, physical garments rather than just a folio of sketches and coursework grades. Two separate work placements are built into the structure, positioned by the university as much for building professional networks in the industry as for skill development.

The course is taught through what TAFE NSW calls a global fashion business lens, meaning students aren't just learning pattern-making and construction but also studying the industry side: trend forecasting, international market awareness, and the commercial context a design has to survive in once it leaves the studio.

As a TAFE NSW degree rather than a standalone art school program, students get access to the technical machinery and production facilities the vocational fashion program uses, which tends to mean more hands-on garment construction time than programs run purely as academic design theory courses.
curriculum:
Core subjects: pattern making and garment construction, textile and fabric knowledge, design fundamentals, fashion illustration, fashion history and trend analysis, global fashion business and market awareness
21 core subjects and 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Two industry work placements across the degree
Third-year capstone: design, construct and present an original fashion collection, submitted alongside a portfolio of realised work
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Fashion Design, portfolio may be requested

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Cyber & Network Security)
description:
TAFE NSW's own bachelor's degree in cyber and network security is a genuinely different animal from its VET certificates in the same subject area. This is a 24-subject, 240-credit-point higher education award, assessed and structured as a degree rather than a training package. What sets it apart from an equivalent university IT degree is where it sits inside the organisation: TAFE NSW runs vocational cyber security qualifications right up to diploma level at the same campuses, so students move through Certificate/Diploma pathways into the bachelor's without changing institutions, and staff teaching the degree often come out of hands-on industry security roles rather than purely academic backgrounds.

The curriculum covers network design, administration and security, with a deliberate emphasis on critical analysis of security risk and applying real mitigation policies rather than treating security as a bolt-on topic within a general IT degree. Cybercrime protection and the use of emerging technologies to manage security threats sit at the centre of the coursework, not the periphery.

For students who want practical, industry-facing training with a straight line to network security and cyber operations roles, without the more theoretical computer science load a traditional university IT degree might carry, this is one of the more targeted options available in NSW.
curriculum:
21 core subjects covering network design and administration, security architecture, cybercrime prevention, data protection, risk analysis and threat management
3 elective subjects, chosen according to specialisation interest and campus availability
Progressive practical labs building toward applied network security projects rather than a single end-of-course assessment
Total: 24 subjects, 240 credit points, delivered as a stand-alone bachelor's degree or via Diploma-to-Bachelor packaged pathway
Not all elective subjects run at every TAFE NSW location each semester
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (TAFE NSW's own published bachelor-entry bar)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Data Engineering)
description:
This is TAFE NSW's data engineering bachelor's, delivered out of the Meadowbank campus, and it's built specifically around the infrastructure and pipeline side of data work: designing, implementing and managing big data systems, rather than the more analysis-and-modelling focus a typical data science degree takes. Students work across data security, cloud computing on both AWS and Microsoft Azure, and emerging database technologies, with the course explicitly designed around industry certification pathways from Cisco, AWS, Microsoft, Red Hat and CompTIA rather than treating certification as an optional extra.

At 24 subjects and 240 credit points over three years, the structure mirrors TAFE NSW's other IT bachelor's degrees, with 21 core subjects and 3 electives, and the practical partnerships with vendors like Palo Alto, Juniper and Oracle mean students are training on tools those companies actually use in production, not generic teaching environments.

Graduates go on to roles like data engineer, SQL developer, cloud data engineer, big data analyst and data warehouse engineer, a more infrastructure-and-pipeline-focused set of outcomes than the model-building and analytics roles a pure data science degree tends to produce.
curriculum:
21 core subjects: data analysis foundations, machine learning fundamentals, AI engineering, data security, networking and infrastructure, cloud computing (AWS and Microsoft Azure), database design and administration, emerging data technologies
3 elective subjects
Industry certification alignment built into coursework (Cisco CCNA, AWS, CompTIA and related vendor pathways)
Total: 24 subjects, 240 credit points, three-year degree, delivered at Meadowbank campus
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway in IT

name: Bachelor of Interior Design
description:
TAFE NSW structures the practical component of this interior design degree in two distinct stages: 70 hours of mandatory work placement earlier in the course, then a compulsory final-year internship in a professional interior design practice that's assessed as its own subject rather than treated as a pass/fail add-on. Students already working in the industry, or those for whom a suitable internship placement can't be found, can substitute one of three alternative electives (sustainability design, total experience design, or lighting interior environments), which is a more flexible arrangement than degrees that make the internship a hard, non-negotiable gate.

Coursework builds from generating original design concepts through to the spatial, structural and material analysis of real interior environments, and the degree deliberately folds in project management and business development skills alongside the creative content, reflecting that most interior designers eventually run or work inside small practices where those business skills matter as much as design talent.

Run through TAFE NSW's Design Centre Enmore, the course emphasises future-focused digital design tools alongside the traditional colour, furniture and fixture specification skills the profession has always required.
curriculum:
Core subjects: design concept generation, spatial and structural analysis, materials and finishes, colour theory and application, furniture and fixture specification, digital design tools and visualisation, project management and business development for designers
70 hours mandatory work placement
Final-year professional internship (compulsory subject) in an interior design practice, or an alternative elective (sustainability design / total experience design / lighting interior environments) where an internship isn't available
Delivered at Design Centre Enmore; total three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Interior Design, portfolio may be requested

name: Bachelor of Property Valuation
description:
TAFE NSW makes a specific, verifiable claim about this degree: it's the only specialist valuation degree in Australia, rather than valuation being taught as a subset within a broader property or business degree elsewhere. It's accredited by the Australian Property Institute (API) for Associate Membership, and graduates with two years of subsequent professional experience become eligible for Certified Practising Valuer (CPV), Certified Property Practitioner (CPP) or Certified Development Practitioner (CDP) status: the actual professional credentials the valuation industry requires for signing off on formal valuations.

At 24 subjects across residential, commercial and specialist valuation areas, the degree is narrower and more technically concentrated than a general property or real estate degree, training students specifically in the methodology, legal frameworks and market analysis techniques a working valuer applies rather than the broader property development, agency or funds-management content a property degree elsewhere might carry.

Given how tightly this program tracks to a single professional credential, it suits students who already know valuation is the specific career they want, rather than those looking for a general property qualification with several possible career exits.
curriculum:
Core subjects: valuation theory and methodology, residential valuation, commercial and industrial valuation, specialist valuation (rural, plant and machinery), property law, real estate economics, statutory valuation and compensation
21 core subjects, 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Capstone valuation practice project, applying methodology across mixed property types
Graduates eligible for API Associate Membership; CPV/CPP/CDP eligibility after two years' professional experience
Total: three-year bachelor's degree, the only specialist valuation degree offered in Australia
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway
